newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen delegation in Asia tour to market natgas.
newsitem.headline: Yemen delegation in Asia tour to market natgas.

text.p: A Yemeni delegation has started a tour of Japan, South Korea, Thailand and Turkey to market the Arab state's liquefied natural gas (LNG) project, an oil official said on Saturday.

The official said the delegation, headed by deputy oil minister Mohieddin al-Dhabi, began the tour two days ago and that talks "will focus on explaining the Yemeni gas project and the prospect of marketing it to these countries".
Yemen's parliament earlier this month approved the $5 billion foreign-backed LNG project which was signed in January.

Under the agreement France's Total SA will take a 36 percent stake in the project, U.S. Exxon Corp jointly with Hunt Oil 30 percent, South Korea's Yukong eight percent and the Yemeni government 26 percent.
First exports from the Yemen Liquefied Natural Gas Co project are slated for 2001 and will have to compete against rival LNG projects in Qatar, Oman and Abu Dhabi for gas markets.
The company plans to produce an annual five million tonnes of LNG.
Presidential approval is required for the project's final go-ahead.
Yemen is a relatively small and independent oil producer.
